title: Object participles
intro: In [B1 unit 5](b1-u05-grammar) the noun after the participle was its subject: *kitap okuyan kız*. When the noun is the object, a place, a time or anything else, Turkish uses `-DIk` with a possessive ending that names the doer: *okuduğum kitap* (the book I'm reading), *oturduğu ev* (the house where she lives). This unit adds the future participle `-(y)AcAk` (*okuyacağım kitap*, *kalacak yer*), the doer in the genitive (*Ali'nin okuduğu kitap*), and a simple test for choosing between `-(y)An` and `-DIk`.

blocks.text: `-DIk` turns a verb into an adjective for anything except its subject. A possessive ending on it names the doer, the way *-ım* names the owner in *kitabım*. *Kitabı okudum* (I read the book) becomes *okuduğum kitap* (the book I read).

blocks.label: From a sentence to a noun phrase
lines: Kitabı okudum.            I read the book.
okuduğum kitap             the book I read
Bu evde oturuyorsun.       You live in this house.
oturduğun ev               the house you live in

blocks.text: `-DIk` follows the harmony and the d/t of the past `-DI` ([A2 unit 1](gp-past-di)): *okuduk-*, *geldik-*, *yaptık-*, *gittik-*. Before the vowel of a possessive ending, its k softens to ğ ([A1 unit 8](gp-consonant-softening)): *okuduğum*, *geldiğin*, *yaptığı*. Before the *-lArI* of **they** it stays: *okudukları*.

blocks.caption: `-DIk` + `-Im` on other verbs
head: Verb
Participle
Example
rows: *gittiğim okul*, the school I go to
*anlamadığım kelime*, the word I don't understand

blocks.text: `-DIk` begins with a consonant, so stems don't change: *gittiğim* (not *gidtiğim*), *yediğim* and *dediğim* (no buffer, no *yi-*). The negative is `-mA` + `-DIk`: *okumadığım kitap*, the book I didn't read.
**Time.** `-DIk` covers the present and the past: *okuduğum kitap* is the book I read, am reading or have read. For the future, use `-(y)AcAk`, in the next section.

**Not just objects.** The noun can be a place, a time, a companion: anything but the subject. *Bir şirkette çalışıyorum* gives *çalıştığım şirket* (the company I work for); *İzmir'de doğdum* gives *doğduğum şehir* (the city I was born in); *O gün tanıştık* gives *tanıştığımız gün* (the day we met). The case of the original sentence disappears, and the noun takes whatever case its own sentence needs: *Oturduğum evi çok seviyorum* (I love the house I live in).

items.en: The book I'm reading is very good.
The film we watched yesterday was very funny.

items.tr: Doğduğum şehir küçük ama çok güzel.
items.seg: Doğ|duğ|um şehir küçük ama çok güzel.
items.en: The city I was born in is small but very beautiful.
The company she works for is in Istanbul.
There's a word I don't understand.
My favourite food is mantı.

blocks.title: En sevdiğim
blocks.text: **My favourite** is *en sevdiğim*, the one I love most: *en sevdiğim şarkı* (my favourite song), *En sevdiğin renk ne?* (What's your favourite colour?). It completes the superlative of [A2 unit 8](gp-superlative).
English can drop **that**: the book (that) I read. French can't: le livre que je lis. Turkish has no word for it at all: the **I** becomes a possessive ending on the participle, *okuduğum*.
The possessive goes on the participle, not on the noun: *okuduğum kitap* (the book I read), never *okuduk kitabım*. *Kitabım* alone means **my book**.

blocks.title: Coming later
blocks.text: With time words `-DIk` gives **when**: *geldiğim zaman* (when I come), and *geldiğimde*, in [B1 unit 8](gp-diginda). As a noun, it reports facts: *Geldiğini biliyorum* (I know that you came), in [B2 unit 4](gp-dik-clauses).

For the future, `-(y)AcAk` takes the place of `-DIk`, with the same possessive endings: *okuyacağım kitap* (the book I'm going to read), *gideceğimiz yer* (the place we'll go to). It is the future of [A2 unit 3](gp-future), with its k softened to ğ before a vowel.

rows.en: (the place) he or she will go to
(the place) you'll go to (plural or polite)

blocks.text: Without a possessive, `-(y)AcAk` describes the subject, as `-(y)An` does: *yarın gelecek misafirler* (the guests who will come tomorrow), *gelecek hafta* (next week, the week to come). It also describes what something is for: *kalacak yer* (a place to stay), *okuyacak bir şey* (something to read), *Yapacak bir şey yok* (There's nothing to do).
Some of these are nouns now: *yiyecek* (food), *içecek* (a drink), *giyecek* (clothing). Menus and signs say *yiyecek ve içecekler* (food and drinks).

items.en: I've chosen the book I'll read on holiday.
The museum we're going to tomorrow is very famous.

items.tr: Bu akşam kalacak bir yer arıyoruz.
items.seg: Bu akşam kal|acak bir yer arıyoruz.
items.en: We're looking for somewhere to stay tonight.

items.tr: Evde yiyecek bir şey var mı?
items.seg: Evde yi|y|ecek bir şey var mı?
items.en: Is there anything to eat at home?

items.tr: Bu köyde yapacak bir şey yok.
items.seg: Bu köyde yap|acak bir şey yok.
items.en: There's nothing to do in this village.
Who are the guests coming tomorrow?

blocks.title: Gideceğim: I'll go, or where I'll go?
blocks.text: *Gideceğim* is the future **I'll go**, and also the participle **(where) I'll go**: the forms are the same. A noun right after it makes it a participle: *Yarın gideceğim* (I'll go tomorrow), *yarın gideceğim yer* (the place I'll go to tomorrow).

sections.title: Ali'nin okuduğu kitap: the doer in the genitive

blocks.text: When the doer is a noun, it goes in the genitive, like an owner, and the participle takes the third-person possessive: *Ali'nin okuduğu kitap* (the book Ali is reading), *annemin yaptığı baklava* (the baklava my mother made). It is the pattern of *Ali'nin kitabı* ([A1 unit 10](gp-genitive-possessive)), with a participle in the place of the possessed noun.

blocks.caption: Doers and participles
head: Doer
Phrase
Meaning
rows: the book my mother is reading
the book the children are reading

blocks.text: **Pronouns** are dropped unless you stress them, as with owners: *okuduğum kitap*, and *benim okuduğum kitap* (the book **I** am reading). **A plural noun** usually takes the singular *-(s)I*: *çocukların okuduğu kitap*, though *çocukların okudukları kitap* is also heard.

items.en: The baklava my mother makes is delicious.
The film Elif recommended was very good.
I've finished the homework the teacher gave us.
Is this the restaurant you meant?
The house our neighbour lives in is very old.

blocks.text: The doer needs the genitive: *Ali'nin okuduğu kitap*, not *Ali okuduğu kitap*. Read it as **Ali's reading-book**: the book belongs to Ali's reading.

sections.title: Okuyan or okuduğu? Choosing the participle

blocks.text: One question decides: **is the noun the subject of the verb in the clause?** If it is, use `-(y)An`. If it is anything else, the object, a place, a time, use `-DIk` (or `-(y)AcAk`) with a possessive for the doer.

English hides the difference: **the man I saw** and **the man who saw me** look alike. Ask who did the seeing. If the man did, he is the subject: *beni gören adam*. If you did, he is the object: *gördüğüm adam*.

The future works the same way: *yarın gelecek misafirler* (the guests who'll come tomorrow: subject, no possessive), *yarın göreceğimiz misafirler* (the guests we'll see tomorrow: object, with a possessive).

items.en: Is there anyone who knows me?
Is there anyone I know?
The people who love you are here.
The people you love are here.
The man I saw yesterday is waiting at the door.

blocks.text: **Whose** is the one exception that looks odd: in *babası doktor olan çocuk* ([B1 unit 5](gp-an-possessor)) the child isn't the subject, his father is, yet the participle is `-(y)An`. That is because the subject, *babası*, sits inside the clause and points to the child.

summary: `-DIk` + possessive describes anything but the subject: *okuduğum kitap*, *oturduğun ev*, *doğduğum şehir*, *tanıştığımız gün*; negative *okumadığım*.
The k softens before a vowel (*okuduğum*) and stays before *-lArI* (*okudukları*); stems don't change (*gittiğim*, *yediğim*).
*En sevdiğim* is **my favourite**: *En sevdiğim yemek mantı*.
For the future, `-(y)AcAk` + possessive: *okuyacağım kitap*, *gideceğimiz yer*; without one, the subject or a purpose: *yarın gelecek misafirler*, *kalacak yer*, *yapacak bir şey yok*.
A noun doer goes in the genitive: *Ali'nin okuduğu kitap*, *annemin yaptığı baklava*.
Choosing: the noun is the subject → `-(y)An` (*beni gören adam*); anything else → `-DIk` (*gördüğüm adam*).
